Q: In an XmlDocument object, how do I make sure a child node of a node list 1) exists and 2) has a value? A:

Yes, it's already answered and accepted. But I would like to add an XmlSerialization solution. This will allow you strong-typing by putting your file's model into actual .NET classes.

First, create a model for the file

Imports System.Xml.Serialization

<XmlRoot("catalog")>
Public Class Catalog
    <XmlElement("book")> Public Property Books As List(Of Book)
End Class

<System.Xml.Serialization.XmlTypeAttribute(AnonymousType:=True)>
Public Class Book
    <XmlAttribute("id")> Public Property ID As String
    <XmlElement("author")> Public Property Author As String
    <XmlElement("title")> Public Property Title As String
    <XmlElement("genre")> Public Property Genre As String
    <XmlElement(ElementName:="price")>
    <DebuggerBrowsable(DebuggerBrowsableState.Never)> Public Property PriceString As String ' we can hide this property from us, but the serializer will use it. Not necessary, but nice to have
        Get
            Return If(Price.HasValue, Price.Value.ToString(), "")
        End Get
        Set(value As String)
            Dim d As Double
            Price = If(Double.TryParse(value, d), d, Nothing)
        End Set
    End Property
    <XmlIgnore> Public Property Price As Double? ' we can see this, but the serializer can't. This is necessary
    <XmlElement(ElementName:="publish_date")> Public Property PublishDate() As Date
    <XmlElement("description")> Public Property Description As String
End Class

And your question is answered in the special handling of price here. The obvious solution is to use IsNullable:=True, however this was not working with all three of your null cases. Serializing the string and exposing a Double? to the program works even better, because it won't write <price xsi:nil="true" /> if you do choose to serialize a null value. With this method you would get <price/>.

From here, the code to read the file, operate on the data, and write the file is much simpler

Dim catalog As Catalog
Dim serializer As New XmlSerializer(GetType(Catalog))
' read the entire file
Using sr As New StreamReader("filename.xml")
    catalog = DirectCast(serializer.Deserialize(sr), Catalog)
End Using
' operate on your data using strong types
For Each book In catalog.Books
    If Not book.Price.HasValue Then
        book.Price = GetPrice(book.ID)
    End If
Next
' write the entire file
Using sw As New StreamWriter("filenameOut.xml")
    serializer.Serialize(sw, catalog)
End Using

If you do have the need to preserve order, the order of the properties in the model defines the order in which the elements are serialized back to the file.

I realize you start with an XmlDocument so this would require a major change to your code. But working with a model like this will pay off as the code is much cleaner and more versatile, as can be seen when comparing how your data is operated on here vs with an XmlDocument.

Q: Excel VBA Copying large array into table takes very long A:

In my testing I see no difference between resizing the listobject prior to placing the data, or letting Excel "autosize" the table after adding the data.

I can say that I've been trying to replicate OP's observations for a while and I do occasionally see cases where the first paste takes a long time and subsequent ones are much faster, but nothing reproducible or where I can see the exact circumstances leading to that.

My testing code:

Sub test()
    Const FRESH_TABLE As Boolean = True
    Const NUM_ROWS As Long = 10000
    Const NUM_COLS As Long = 34
    
    Dim ws As Worksheet, data, tbl As ListObject, t, n As Long, msg, hdrs
    
    Set ws = Sheet1
    ReDim hdrs(1 To 1, 1 To NUM_COLS)
    For n = 1 To NUM_COLS
        hdrs(1, n) = "Col" & Format(n, "000")
    Next n
    
    If FRESH_TABLE Then
        ws.Cells.Clear
        ws.Range("a1").Resize(1, NUM_COLS).Value = hdrs
        Set tbl = ws.ListObjects.Add(xlSrcRange, _
                      ws.Range("a1").Resize(1, NUM_COLS), , xlYes)
    Else
        Set tbl = ws.ListObjects(1)
    End If
                  
    DoEvents
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    
    EmptyTable tbl
    DoEvents
    
    For Each msg In Array("X", "T") 'trying different data... 
        data = GetData(CStr(msg), NUM_ROWS, NUM_COLS) 'get some dummy data
        Debug.Print msg & String(10, "-")
        For n = 1 To 3
            t = Timer
            AddArrayToTable tbl, data
            Debug.Print n, Round(Timer - t, 3)
        Next n
    Next msg
End Sub

'Clear listobject `tbl`
Sub EmptyTable(tbl As ListObject)
    If tbl.ListRows.Count > 0 Then
        tbl.DataBodyRange.ClearContents
        tbl.Resize tbl.Range.Rows(1).Resize(2)
    End If
End Sub

'Return a 1-based 2D array of size `nRows` x `nCols`
Function GetData(msg As String, nRows As Long, nCols As Long)
    Dim r As Long, c As Long, data
    
    ReDim data(1 To nRows, 1 To nCols)
    For r = 1 To nRows
        For c = 1 To nCols
            data(r, c) = Join(Array(msg, r, c), "~")
        Next
    Next
    GetData = data
End Function

Sub AddArrayToTable(tbl As ListObject, data)
    Dim cDest As Range, lrCount As Long
    Dim nR As Long, nC As Long

    nR = UBound(data, 1)
    nC = UBound(data, 2)
    lrCount = tbl.ListRows.Count
    
    If lrCount = 0 Then 'any existing rows?
        Set cDest = tbl.Range.Cells(2, 1)
    Else
        Set cDest = tbl.ListRows(lrCount).Range.Cells(1).Offset(1)
    End If
    'following line seems to make no difference to performance
    tbl.Resize cDest.Parent.Range(tbl.Range.Cells(1), cDest.Offset(nR - 1, nC - 1))
    cDest.Resize(nR, nC).Value = data
End Sub

One weird thing I noticed was that dummy data values starting with "X" take longer to add than values of the same length starting with "T". Go figure.

Q: Specify argument and return types of dict transpose function A:

To define a transposable dictionary type and its transposition type, please use TypeVar from the typing module. Please try the below code:

from collections import defaultdict
from typing import TypeVar, Dict, Set

# Define type variables for the keys and values
K = TypeVar('K')
V = TypeVar('V')

def transpose_dict(dct: Dict[K, Set[V]]) -> Dict[V, Set[K]]:
    transposed = defaultdict(set)

    for key, value_set in dct.items():
        for inv_key in value_set:
            transposed[inv_key].add(key)
            
    return transposed

For modern Python, you will probably want to use type parameter lists (3.12+) and subscripted builtins (3.9+) instead of constructs from the typing module:

from collections import defaultdict

def transpose_dict[K, V](dct: dict[K, set[V]]) -> dict[V, set[K]]:
    transposed = defaultdict(set)

    for key, value_set in dct.items():
        for inv_key in value_set:
            transposed[inv_key].add(key)

    return transposed
